Lessons.Title: Symmetry in Figures (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will identify figures with line symmetry and to complete line-symmetric figures.
Previously, you learned to identify figures with line symmetry and drew lines of symmetry. In this lesson, you deepen your understanding of symmetry by reasoning about what the whole figure would look like when given half of a figure and a line of symmetry. The work of this lesson helps you develop mental images of figures with lines of symmetry.

2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up: Number Talk: Keeping Track (10 minutes); Activity 1: Half-drawn Figures (15 minutes); Activity 2: What’s the Whole Picture? (20 minutes); Activity 3: What Could the Whole Figure Be? [OPTIONAL] (10 minutes); Cool-down: Make Them Whole (5 minutes)
Source-goal geometric reasoning: Complete a line-symmetric figure by placing every missing point or segment at equal perpendicular distance on the opposite side of the axis.

Edulytics worked explanation: Locate the given symmetry axis on the actual source drawing. Count perpendicular grid squares from each existing vertex to the axis. Reflect each vertex to the other side at the same distance, then connect corresponding vertices. Check that both halves coincide under a fold.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (not gated original): On grid paper, draw the missing half of a triangle reflected across a dashed vertical line.
Original student diagrams, teacher card sorting, paper folding, and physical drawings require figure-by-figure / teacher validation.
